claims: C1 default instructions exist because deriving answers from higher-level principles on the fly is impractical and makes model behavior less predictable
C2 specifying answers as guidelines that can be overridden improves predictability and reliability
C3 specifying answers as guidelines leaves developers flexibility to remove or adapt the instructions in their applications

concepts.name: guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: the guideline level of instruction authority: instructions that can be implicitly overridden

concepts.name: default_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that specifies an answer to a question the model would otherwise have to derive from higher-level principles

concepts.name: overridable_guideline
concepts.gloss: an instruction that can be overridden implicitly, i.e. a guideline rather than a strict requirement

concepts.name: developer_flexible_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that can be removed or adapted by developers in their applications

ontology.gloss: I is a default instruction because it carries guideline authority
I is an overridable guideline because it carries guideline authority
I is a developer-flexible instruction because it carries guideline authority
